source_observations.observation: Support case, continuation and termination of plain ya, scope of yat and gha, own sense, maker, state and supplementary rules.
Relative ye and brāhmaṇās before somyās teṣām. The next negative genitive asomyasya contrasts exclusion from the offering.

source_observations.locator: Śākala RV 8.24.13, Saṃhitā, Pada, Sāyaṇa and annotations
source_observations.observation: Pada separates somyam and madhu. Sāyaṇa construes the drink as made of Soma. The morph annotation labels the adjective NOM but madhu ACC.
Madhavyān agrees with stokān. The grammatical commentary identifies the composition as honey.

source_observations.locator: Śaunaka 7.27.8 with Pada and Sāyaṇa; permanent revision 339065
source_observations.observation: Pada vasavyaiḥ with bahubhiḥ. Sāyaṇa names collections of goods and cites 4.4.140.

source_observations.locator: Śākala RV 4.55.8 with Pada and Sāyaṇa
source_observations.observation: Genitive vasavyasya governed by īśe. The commentator explains an aggregate of riches.
Five formula counts are 4,4,2,5,2. The next identification names Prajāpati as seventeenfold in the sacrifice.

source_observations.locator: Mādhyandina Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā 22.28 with Uvaṭa and Mahīdhara
source_observations.observation: Two consecutive svāhā clauses independently supply the simple and extended star datives.
Sarvatātim is the single object of suvatu, glossed as all that is desired.
Devá-tātim is singular in form. Sāyaṇa glosses it with plural devān and explicitly assigns tātil and its accent.

source_observations.locator: Śākala RV 8.18.7, Pada, Sāyaṇa and Jamison–Brereton notes
source_observations.observation: Short śaṃtāti. Sāyaṇa takes a peace-bringing modifier of mayas. Competing proposals include a neuter noun and an indeclinable.
Pada records the long dual. Sāyaṇa assigns two makers of welfare to the two Aśvins under 4.4.143.

source_observations.locator: Śākala RV 10.60.7–9, Pada and comment on verse 8
source_observations.observation: The repeated purpose dative is ariṣṭatātaye. Sāyaṇa calls the suffix svārthika, while Vasu adduces the refrain in the maker discussion.
The repeated nominative precedes astu. The apparatus identifies K as writing the refrain at the specified interior verses.

source_observations.locator: Paippalāda 5.18.2ab, GRETIL version 1 and Bhattacharya apparatus
source_observations.observation: Two coordinated instrumentals with come to you. The edition distinguishes its nasal notation from Bhattacharya’s first reading.
